title: Introduction to Software Engineering
description: The CCMAS introduction to software engineering: software engineering as a discipline, software process models, agile development and Extreme Programming, requirements engineering, design with UML and architectural design, validation and testing, and evolution, maintenance, re-engineering and project management. Built from the SEN 201 lecture notes and class notes in the course folder.

topics.title: Software Engineering as a Discipline
topics.summary: Software engineering is the application of a systematic, disciplined, quantifiable approach to the development, operation and maintenance of software. It arose from the 1960s software crisis, uses abstraction and decomposition, and aims for maintainable, dependable, efficient and acceptable software.
subtopics: The software crisis and the NATO conference
Generic and bespoke products; attributes of good software
Types of application and the fundamental principles

topics.title: Software Processes and Process Models
topics.summary: A software process is a sequence of activities, specification, development, validation and evolution, that produces software. Process models include the plan-driven waterfall model, incremental development, reuse-oriented engineering, prototyping, incremental delivery and Boehm's risk-driven spiral model.

topics.title: Agile Development and Extreme Programming
topics.summary: Agile methods are incremental methods with small increments released every two or three weeks, built on customer involvement, incremental delivery, people not process, embracing change and simplicity. Extreme Programming takes incremental development to an extreme with user stories, pair programming and test-first development.

topics.title: Requirements Engineering
topics.summary: Requirements engineering discovers, analyses, documents and maintains what a system should do and its constraints. Its activities are feasibility study, elicitation and analysis, specification and validation; requirements are user or system, and functional or non-functional, recorded in the SRS.
subtopics: User and system requirements; functional and non-functional

topics.title: Software Design, UML and Architectural Design
topics.summary: Software design describes the structure, data, interfaces and sometimes algorithms of the software; its activities are architectural, interface, component and database design. Object-oriented design uses UML structural and dynamic models, and architectural design defines the system's overall organisation in four views.
subtopics: Architectural, interface, component and database design

topics.title: Software Validation and Testing
topics.summary: Verification and validation show that a system conforms to its specification and meets the customer's expectations. Testing has two goals, validation and defect testing; development testing works at unit, component and system level, and user testing includes alpha, beta and acceptance testing.
subtopics: Development testing: unit, component and system
User testing: alpha, beta and acceptance
The six stages of acceptance testing

topics.title: Evolution, Maintenance, Re-engineering and Project Management
topics.summary: Software must keep changing after delivery to stay useful, through change analysis, release planning, implementation and release. Maintenance is fault repair, environmental adaptation or functionality addition; legacy systems may be re-engineered; and project management plans, organises and controls projects and teams.
